Meet Me on the Landing
Two doors, eleven feet apart, and a war fought entirely in sticky notes.
An audio editor and a building surveyor keep misreading each other's door notes — until one of them says the load-bearing words out loud.

Naomi edits a comedy audio drama from her fourth-floor walk-up; Graham, across the landing, surveys buildings for a living and reads every note like a structural report. A noise complaint aimed at the wrong neighbor, a prop love letter in the wrong mailbox, and a listening session he mistakes for a work request keep them guessing. Over eight chapters you decide what Naomi says to his face — and whether either of them needs a note ever again.
The neighbor in 4C, who reads every note on both doors before either of them does.
If they keep talking in notes, they stay perfectly polite strangers who could have been something — and the landing gets awkward for everyone.
